completion_data.completion_summary: Shipped census-count.sh (occurrences/membership/cross-check subcommands mapping to the three named repo-wide-count bug classes), two fixture-driven regression suites (21 and 8 cases, both passing with a confirmed mutation check), a fixed separator-aware regex in validate-no-task-references.sh (with a task-qualified compound Phase branch), and two new standards docs (shell-script-testing.md, census-methodology.md), all registered in manifest.json and index-entries.json.

memory_candidates.content: For a bash regex fixture suite whose whole point is proving a regex fix, add a one-time mutation check: revert the fix, re-run the suite, confirm it goes red, then restore. A suite that passes unchanged against both the old and new pattern provides zero regression protection for the gap the fix closed -- this is the anti-vacuous-test guard applied to string/regex fixes specifically (parallel to 'a naive-vs-correct fixture pair, never a happy-path-only fixture' for tool behavior).

When a hook or advisory script's own source comments contain concrete example strings illustrating a pattern it detects, dogfood the finished script against its own file content before closing the task. A pattern-detection script's explanatory comments can accidentally match its own detection regex if they use concrete example values (e.g. a digit sequence) instead of letter placeholders (N, P, M) -- self-referential false positives are easy to miss without an explicit self-check pass.

manifest.json's provides.context array lists directory names (e.g. "standards", "formats"), not individual file paths -- adding a new file under an already-listed context/ subdirectory needs only an index-entries.json entry, no manifest.json change. Verify this by checking for any .md-suffixed path entry under the target subdirectory before assuming a manifest edit is needed.
